intention: Every internal/ module that owns persistence gets its own Postgres schema, making the modular-monolith boundary visible in the database and checkable at sqlc codegen time.
request: schema per module for internal/ modules

decisions.decision: Additive migrations (CREATE SCHEMA + ALTER TABLE ... SET SCHEMA), not rewritten history
decisions.why: 4 new files vs ~25 edited; needs no db-reset; leaves charging's backfill migration working
Forced, not chosen: sqlc fails codegen on a bare name once the table leaves public. Verified by repro.

decisions.decision: gen.go.rename with singularized keys keeps all 12 Go type names unchanged
decisions.why: Schema-qualifying renames every struct, churning ~144 call sites. Wrong key form fails silently, exit 0.

decisions.decision: goose unchanged; shared public.goose_db_version kept; migration-guard NOT retired
decisions.why: Version collisions are independent of table schemas. Keeps the roadmap reset-free. Follow-up is backlog #23.

Supersedes D5. Two tables both named *_sessions was the owner's actual confusion; a fleet_ prefix leaves both called 'sessions'. _history not _snapshots because this table is upserted as Tesla settles fees, while vehicle_snapshots is append-only -- calling both 'snapshots' invites a double-counting query. Matches the dx/charging/history endpoint.

The old name over-claims: the table is a Supercharger-only dense mirror that originates no value, yet reads as all charging, and analytics treats it and manual_charge_entries as two separate watermark sources. Reuses the name D5a frees -- accepted hazard: 133 doc files and frozen archived specs still use it for telemetry's table. Supported by RM31 D8, which already chose 'Supercharger' vocabulary inside charging.

decisions.decision: Generated Go type names follow the tables; NOT frozen (opposite of D3)
decisions.why: The renames exist to remove stale vocabulary, so freezing Go names would half-fix the confusion in the most-read code. Consequence: SuperchargerSession moves telemetry->charging rather than being renamed. Verified safe -- charging never imports telemetry.SuperchargerSession, so the swap crosses no import edge.

decisions.decision: Tier 4 blocked; charging's cross-module backfill read is fixed under a separate ticket
decisions.why: Owner chose to fix the boundary violation outside RM39. Tier 4 breaks charging tests A1/A2 until it lands.

decisions.decision: Tier 3 orders its migration CREATE SCHEMA -> SET SCHEMA -> RENAME TO
decisions.why: Tier 3 runs before tier 4, so telemetry still holds public.supercharger_sessions; renaming charging's table first collides. Moving the schema first lets both coexist -- and frees D5b from the D6 block.

decisions.decision: The rename DELETEs the affected vehicle_metric_watermarks rows
decisions.why: Post-rename the CHECK set is byte-identical to the pre-20260828000001 set, when 'supercharger_sessions' meant telemetry's table -- same string, two meanings by era, and Recalculator keys its cursor on it. A missing row means epoch per the table's own contract, so deleting is self-healing. Data loss acceptable (MAG-31).

decisions.decision: Every tier must also schema-qualify the raw SQL in its _test.go files (new work-shape step 2b)
decisions.why: Tier 1 shipped with query.sql qualified and every Claude-runnable signal clean, yet 10 integration tests failed: sqlc never sees test SQL strings and go vet treats them as strings.

tiers.notes: Pilot tier. 3 tables, no cross-module reads. Establishes the pattern later tiers mirror.

3 tables. Watermark 'source' string values must NOT be schema-qualified; a CHECK constraint depends on them. Plus work-shape step 2b (D9): schema-qualify ~5 raw SQL statements in this module's _test.go files.

2 tables. ALSO renames charge_sessions -> supercharger_sessions (D5b) in the same migration, with the mandatory D7 statement order (CREATE SCHEMA -> SET SCHEMA -> RENAME TO). Renames ChargeSession -> SuperchargerSession, 2 sqlc query names, the index and the pct_source constraint. Deletes watermark rows (D8). Must not touch the backfill migration. Corrects kkpa/context KB, which is stale since RM38/RM40. Plus work-shape step 2b (D9): schema-qualify ~15 raw SQL statements in this module's _test.go files.

PRECEDED BY GATE G1 (owner-run make db-reset). BLOCKED on the external boundary ticket (D6). 4 tables. ALSO renames supercharger_sessions -> supercharger_history (D5a) and the db model + hand-written domain type to SuperchargerHistory, plus 5 sqlc query names. Public port SuperchargerReader stays put -- that is tier 5. Landing it breaks charging tests A1/A2. Plus work-shape step 2b (D9): schema-qualify ~19 raw SQL statements in this module's _test.go files.

No schema change. Finishes D5c by renaming telemetry's public port (SuperchargerReader, its 4 methods, NewSuperchargerReader and the internal helpers). Split from tier 4 deliberately: 88 references outside internal/telemetry, across charging, analytics, gateway, app and both cmd/ binaries. Mechanical and compiler-checked.

found pre-existing KB debt: kkpa/context/architecture/telemetry-data-hub.md still shows the gateway reading telemetry.Reader, which RM38/RM40 removed and make boundary-guard now forbids. Correction assigned to tier 3.
added blocking owner-run gate G1 (make db-reset) between tiers 3 and 4, at the owner's request: RM39 preserves all data by design, so a fresh-data wipe must be explicit.

audited the Makefile against the schema move: zero schema/public/GRANT/search_path references, zero bare table names, no guard reads SQL. db-setup migrates AS the app role against a role-owned database, so CREATE SCHEMA makes that role the schema owner -- no GRANT and no search_path change needed. No make target requires updating; the per-tier obligation is the goose Down reversing in opposite order.

gates.name: database reset for fresh test data
gates.why: The owner wants a clean database to start testing on fresh data (MAG-31). RM39 preserves every row by design (D1/D4 use catalog-only ALTER TABLE ... SET SCHEMA / RENAME TO), so a wipe cannot happen as a side effect and must be an explicit gate.
gates.placement_why: After tier 3 because tiers 1-3 are the unblocked run and tier 4 waits on the D6 boundary ticket. Also avoids re-establishing the Tesla connection twice.
post_steps: reconnect Tesla through cmd/web -- db-reset drops accounts and tesla_tokens
run the poller once, then verify the pages render
